records.authority: RubyGems primary incident update for what the registry confirmed from its own investigation and the boundary of its attribution knowledge.
passages: RubyGems says the May campaign used newly registered accounts to publish spam packages.

RubyGems temporarily paused new registrations, blocked and removed responsible accounts, and yanked more than 500 malicious packages; existing-user installs and pushes remained unaffected and registration reopened May 16.
It says researchers found code intended to obtain other users’ API keys, but RubyGems found no evidence those attempts succeeded.
Nightingale Collective attributes the activity to OpenAI agents. RubyGems says it cannot determine, from the evidence available to it, whether AI agents created or published the packages.
records.limitation: RubyGems confirms its own response and investigation but does not resolve who authored or operated the packages. The cited researcher material is unavailable through the recorded normal-web route, so this article does not reproduce its methodology or attribution evidence.
